name: Question 15
problem:
The second-order differential equation ${y}^{″}-4{y}^{′}+3y=0$
can be expressed as the matrix equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where 

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}],\,y(t)={x}_{1}(t),\,{y}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t).
$$

Find the matrix $A.$
worked_solution:
We first need to express the given differential equation as a system of first-order differential equations. Then, we write the system as a matrix equation.

We start by making the following change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =y \\ {x}_{2} & ={y}^{′}\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the above equations with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′} & ={y}^{′} \\ {x}_{2}^{′} & ={y}^{″}\end{aligned}
$$

which we can rewrite as 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2}, \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={y}^{″}.\end{aligned}
$$

We must now write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}.$

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative $({y}^{″}),$ we obtain

$$
{y}^{″}=4{y}^{′}-3y.
$$

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives

$$
{y}^{″}=4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{1}.
$$

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side. 

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}=-3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can represent this system as the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence, $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}].$

Question 15

The second-order differential equation y″−4y′+3y=0 can be expressed as the matrix equation x′(t)=Ax(t), where

x(t)=[x1x2],A=[abcd],y(t)=x1(t),y′(t)=x2(t). Find the matrix A.

a
[41−30]
b
[014−3]
c
[01−34]
d
[−3104]
e
[01−30]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We first need to express the given differential equation as a system of first-order differential equations. Then, we write the system as a matrix equation.

We start by making the following change of variables: x1=yx2=y′

Differentiating the above equations with respect to t, we get x1′=y′x2′=y″

which we can rewrite as

{x1′=x2,x2′=y″.

We must now write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of x1 and x2.

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative (y″), we obtain y″=4y′−3y.

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives y″=4x2−3x1. Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows: {x1′=x2x2′=−3x1+4x2

We can represent this system as the matrix differential equation x′(t)=Ax(t) as follows: [x1′x2′]=[01−34][x1x2].

Hence, A=[01−34].
